issues.title: [Rescue/Zero-Trust] Implement revision-bound Repair Capsule without GitHub write access
issues.evidence: Baseline `main`: `0afd83557cd222d0174e71ceb52feb737fa7db99`. Sovereign Rescue already owns revision-bound diagnosis, isolated repair workspaces, real diff/test evidence, Outcome Contracts, a 12-file limit, secret redaction and ProofPack logic. The missing product surface is a delivery mode that gives the customer a locally verifiable patch without granting Sovereign GitHub write access. Related existing work: #1100 and #1113; neither is treated as completed by this issue.
issues.goal: Add one bounded Sovereign Rescue delivery mode that returns `repair.patch`, `manifest.json`, `verify.py` and `README.md`. The customer verifies and applies the patch locally. Product promise: `Lass deine Software von einer KI reparieren, ohne ihr Schreibzugriff auf dein Repository zu geben.` Re-resolve the exact current `main` SHA before implementation.
rules: No automatic apply and no GitHub write token in Capsule mode.
No branch, commit, PR, merge, deployment or customer database migration from Capsule delivery.
Bind every Capsule to an exact Git base SHA, deterministic canonical hashes, the real workspace diff, real targeted test evidence and at most 12 changed files.
Derive patch paths from patch bytes and require exact identity with persisted changed-file evidence.
Fail closed on secrets, traversal, absolute paths, `.git/`, binary patches, submodules, unsafe symlink or mode changes and unknown diff features.
Do not claim production health, CI green, applied patch, digital signature or runtime success without corresponding real evidence.
Mocks, stubs, fake repositories, fake heads, UI flags and workflow tricks cannot satisfy product acceptance.
workflow: Re-resolve current `main` and inventory canonical Rescue, diff, workspace, route and mirror ownership.
Implement and review the pure Capsule contract and offline verifier first.
Add the tenant-safe zero-write delivery route and explicit frontend mode.
Run real sandbox acceptance for CI, Docker Compose and PostgreSQL failure families plus one unsupported case.
Record observed benchmark values and release only if every zero-write security invariant holds.
integrationPlan: Keep pure-core construction separate from effect adapters and UI.
Reuse existing Outcome Contract, repair row, job evidence, diff tool, secret redaction and max-file boundary instead of duplicating truth.
Use separate PRs for core, delivery/UI and real evidence if they cannot be reviewed safely together.
Do not add persistent patch/blob storage in PostgreSQL; persist only identities or hashes if later justified by a separate migration.
acceptance: Capsule delivery performs zero GitHub writes and requires no GitHub write credential.
A fresh clone at the exact base SHA passes `verify.py` and `git apply --check` before explicit local apply.
After local apply, the same real targeted checks used in the repair workspace are rerun and recorded.
Base-SHA mismatch, patch-hash mismatch, path mismatch, traversal, secret material or unsupported diff feature blocks delivery.
The unsupported application-bug case produces no successful Capsule.

issues.title: [Rescue/Capsule Core] Build deterministic manifest, secure diff parser, and local verifier
issues.evidence: Part of the Zero-Trust Repair Capsule program. Baseline `main`: `0afd83557cd222d0174e71ceb52feb737fa7db99`. Existing Rescue core already normalizes revisions, changed files, secrets and canonical SHA-256 values, but it does not yet construct a portable patch package or independently parse and validate unified-diff paths.
issues.goal: Implement only the deterministic, side-effect-free `sovereign.repair-capsule.v1` contract, a secure unified-diff parser and an offline local verifier. Re-resolve current `main` before coding. This issue must introduce no API, UI or GitHub mutation.
paths: canonical mirror/contract tests required by the current repository ownership model
rules: Manifest fields include repair ID, hashed repository identity, base SHA, failure family, Outcome Contract SHA-256, ordered changed paths, patch SHA-256, test-evidence SHA-256, max changed files, `productionMutationIncluded=false`, blockers, ready and canonical Capsule SHA-256.
Patch paths come from parsed patch bytes, never solely from agent-reported `changedFiles`.
Block absolute paths, `..`, `.git/`, empty patches, more than 12 paths, path-set mismatch, secret-shaped content, binary patches, submodules, unsafe symlink/mode changes and unknown diff syntax.
`verify.py` is deterministic and offline: check local HEAD, manifest hash, patch hash, exact path set and `git apply --check`; do not access a network or apply the patch automatically.
Timestamp or archive metadata must not make identical evidence produce different canonical hashes.
Canonical and deployment mirror implementations remain byte-identical or pass the repository's explicit mirror contract.
workflow: Inventory the current diff format and all supported file-change classes.
Define strict manifest and parser contracts with closed schemas.
Implement deterministic builder and verifier generation.
Add adversarial parser and hash tests.
Run canonical/mirror and existing Rescue contract suites.
integrationPlan: Reuse `normalize_head_sha`, `normalize_repair_changed_files`, `redact_secret_text`, `canonical_sha256` and the existing max-file boundary where canonical.
Separate path parsing from manifest assembly so both can be tested without filesystem or GitHub access.
Treat rename, delete, new-file, mode, symlink, submodule and binary changes as explicitly supported or explicitly blocked; never silently accept.
Document the exact supported unified-diff subset.
issues.example:
assert parsed_paths(patch_bytes) == manifest["changedFiles"]
assert sha256(patch_bytes) == manifest["patchSha256"]
assert local_git_head(repo) == manifest["baseSha"]
run(["git", "apply", "--check", "repair.patch"])
acceptance: Same evidence produces the same manifest and Capsule SHA-256.
One changed patch byte or base SHA changes the corresponding identity and fails verification.
All traversal, secret, binary, submodule, unsafe symlink/mode and unknown-feature fixtures fail closed.
Ordering, Unicode and path edge cases are deterministic and adversarially tested.
No network, API, UI, GitHub write or repository publication effect is added.

issues.title: [Rescue/Capsule Delivery] Add tenant-safe download API and explicit zero-write user flow
issues.evidence: Part of the Zero-Trust Repair Capsule program. Baseline `main`: `0afd83557cd222d0174e71ceb52feb737fa7db99`. Rescue already exposes tenant-scoped diagnosis, repair and ProofPack routes plus a frontend panel. A dedicated Capsule route and user flow are needed so patch delivery remains distinct from Draft-PR publication.
issues.goal: Add a tenant-safe, bounded Capsule download endpoint and explicit frontend choice between Draft PR and Zero-Trust Capsule. Re-resolve current `main` before coding. Capsule delivery must accept no GitHub write credential and must perform no GitHub write.
rules: Use `POST /api/user/agent/rescue/repairs/<repair_id>/capsule` or the canonically equivalent owner route.
Read only tenant-owned repair, job and workspace evidence.
Return a bounded attachment containing exactly the approved Capsule files.
Do not require or accept a GitHub token for Capsule delivery.
Do not branch, commit, push, create a PR, merge, deploy, migrate a customer database or apply to a customer repository.
Use ephemeral generation or bounded artifact storage; do not persist raw source, patches, archives, secrets or model output in PostgreSQL.
Enforce session, CSRF, tenant ownership, content type, size limit, same-evidence idempotency, workspace-diff identity and stale-evidence blocking.
UI must show exact base SHA and never claim applied patch, green CI or healthy production.
workflow: Bind the route to the canonical Capsule core output.
Add tenant/session/CSRF and bounded-download contracts.
Add explicit Draft PR versus Zero-Trust Capsule selection in the Rescue UI.
Add negative and accessibility tests.
Verify through real route readback that Capsule mode performs zero GitHub writes.
integrationPlan: Keep Draft-PR publication unchanged and visibly separate.
Reuse existing repair/job tenancy and CSRF boundaries.
Do not add a database migration in v1 unless reproducibility cannot be achieved from existing persisted evidence; any migration requires separate review.
Return explicit blockers rather than partial archives.
issues.example:
POST /api/user/agent/rescue/repairs/<repair_id>/capsule
Authorization: existing session
X-Sovereign-Rescue-CSRF: <bound token>
Response: attachment; no githubAccessToken field accepted
acceptance: Cross-tenant access is denied without leaking identifiers or Capsule bytes.
Frontend sends no GitHub token and backend invokes no write-capable GitHub method.
Repeated requests over identical evidence return identical manifest and patch hashes.
Changed/stale workspace diff, oversized output or missing test evidence blocks the download.
Draft-PR and Capsule modes never share a misleading success state.

issues.title: [Rescue/Capsule Evidence] Prove zero-write repair delivery with real sandbox repositories and benchmark it
issues.evidence: Part of the Zero-Trust Repair Capsule program. Baseline `main`: `0afd83557cd222d0174e71ceb52feb737fa7db99`. Unit and adapter tests can validate contracts, but they cannot prove the product promise that a real repair can be delivered, verified and applied locally with zero GitHub writes.
issues.goal: Produce revision-bound real acceptance evidence and an observed-value benchmark for Capsule delivery using disposable or owner-approved GitHub repositories. Re-resolve current `main` before execution. No mock, fake head, fake CI, UI flag or workflow trick may satisfy acceptance.
paths: real sandbox repositories for GitHub Actions/CI, Docker Compose and PostgreSQL migration failures
real repair workspace, diff and targeted-test evidence
versioned benchmark/evidence documentation under the canonically selected docs path
rules: For each supported case read the real GitHub base SHA, diagnose, repair in an isolated workspace, run real targeted tests, produce real `git diff`, create Capsule, clone fresh at the exact base SHA, run `verify.py`, run `git apply --check`, apply locally, rerun the same tests and read back paths/hashes.
The unsupported application-bug case must fail closed without a successful Capsule.
Record observed values only; do not invent targets or transfer competitor metrics.
Compare Capsule and existing Draft-PR delivery without changing either result definition.
Security invariants must remain zero: Capsule GitHub writes, automatic applies, accepted traversal, accepted base-SHA mismatch, secret output and accepted changed-file mismatch.
Unit mocks may test adapters only and never count as product proof.
workflow: Create or select four real disposable/owner-approved repositories and record exact identities.
Execute supported Rescue flows and unsupported fail-closed flow.
Run fresh-clone verification and local apply sequence.
Read back GitHub, workspace, test and artifact identities.
Publish an observed-value comparison and unresolved limitations.
integrationPlan: Measure verifier success, apply-check success, targeted-test parity, required permissions, GitHub write count, hash/SHA/path rejections and time to locally verifiable repair versus Draft PR.
Where user testing is available, measure mode selection, permission-dialog abandonment and support incidents; otherwise mark these as not yet observed.
Bind evidence to exact repository and Capsule identities.
Block release if any zero-valued security invariant is violated.
issues.example:
assert capsule.github_write_count == 0
assert fresh_clone.head_sha == manifest.baseSha
assert verifier.ok
assert git_apply_check.ok
assert targeted_tests_after_apply == targeted_tests_in_repair_workspace
acceptance: All three supported real cases produce locally verifiable Capsules with zero GitHub writes.
The unsupported case fails closed and yields no successful Capsule.
Fresh-clone path/hash/SHA readbacks and real targeted tests are recorded for every supported case.
Benchmark report contains observed values or explicit `not measured`, never invented numbers.
Any violated security invariant blocks release.
